title: Context API Core Check
description: Check your understanding of prop drilling, context creation, providers, useContext, and context best practices.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What problem does React Context primarily help solve?

options.text: Sharing values through a component subtree without passing props at every level

questions.explanation: Context is useful when many descendants need the same value and prop drilling becomes awkward.

questions.prompt: Prop drilling is always bad and should always be replaced with context.
questions.explanation: Passing props is often explicit and simple. Context is best when shared access improves clarity.

questions.prompt: Which component makes a context value available to descendants?
questions.explanation: A Provider supplies the value that descendants can read from the context.

options.text: The nearest matching provider value above the component
A setter for the provider only
The default value even when a provider exists

questions.explanation: useContext reads the value from the closest matching provider in the component tree.

questions.prompt: Which values are common fits for context? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Every keystroke of a local form field

questions.explanation: Theme, auth user, and locale are commonly shared across a subtree; local form input often belongs near the form.

questions.prompt: Why might a custom hook wrap useContext?

options.text: To centralize provider-missing checks and simplify imports
To make context update synchronously before render
To mutate the context default value

questions.explanation: A custom hook can provide a clean API and throw a helpful error when used outside its provider.

questions.prompt: Why split one large context into smaller contexts?

options.text: To group values with different change patterns and reduce unnecessary consumers updates
To remove the need for state

questions.explanation: Separating slow-changing and fast-changing values can keep unrelated consumers from updating together.

questions.prompt: Provider value identity can matter for performance when many consumers depend on the context.
questions.explanation: A newly created object or function value can notify consumers more often than intended.
